# Architecture guide

## Current system

Orders, Shipments, Inventory, Sales, Expenses, HR and LINE own their business
workflows. Shared infrastructure owns provider transports and PostgreSQL sessions;
composition wires feature-owned ports. `src/externals/` and `src/features/` are
retired. Supported service/script compatibility remains explicit.

Production's last verified application release is PR87/88 `296529d`: all 23 business tables use
native `deletedAt`, with 67 lifecycle timestamps including media, 61 operational
functions and 52 triggers. LINE remained open during that application-only release.
Operational cell/ordinal/kind/lexeme sidecars and duplicate media URLs are gone.
Old business Sheets remain read-only; Drive and private integration accounts keep
their existing ownership. This records the last checkpoint, not a fresh live read.

Business storage uses PostgreSQL-only named-record adapters. This branch retires
the remaining Sheets configuration reader in favor of private PostgreSQL accounts.
Each feature owns its explicit column maps and semantic port adapters;
root transport owns SQL, transactions and private ID/revision handles. Worksheet
classes, range/header repair, the aggregate Sheets business service and its runtime
fallback are retired. Google Drive uploads and the fixed read-only account
configuration remain. Existing public report type names are retained API contracts.
This source work does not deploy, alter the schema or authorize a live change.
See [verification](../refactoring/verification.md), [operations](../database-migration.md)
and the [evidence ledger](../refactoring/progress.md#latest-production-release).

New staff authentication/RBAC/shop permissions and backup automation remain deferred.
Existing access controls are preserved; migration completion is not an access-
control certification. Future live changes require their own approval.

## Find the right document

| Question | Authoritative source |
| --- | --- |
| Where do files belong and which dependencies are allowed? | [Architecture rules](rules.md) |
| Who owns current modules, worksheets and compatibility paths? | [Ownership map](migration-map.md) |
| Which observable contracts must remain stable? | [Architecture decisions](decisions.md) |
| How is production stored, recovered and maintained? | [Supabase operations](../database-migration.md) |
| What is the next authorized scope? | [Roadmap](../refactoring/roadmap.md) |
| Which PR/CI/release proves a result? Where is older evidence? | [Evidence ledger](../refactoring/progress.md) |
| How are local/CI checks run safely? | [Verification guide](../refactoring/verification.md) |
| How should work be prepared and reviewed? | [Engineering rules](../../AGENTS.md) |
| What is planned for staff access? | [Authentication roadmap](user-authentication-roadmap.md) |

## Feature guides

[Expenses](../expenses.md), [movements](../movement-migration.md),
[stock adjustments](../shop-stock-adjustments.md) and
[LINE menu links](../rich-menu-links.md) keep their established paths. Their feature
workflows and historical Sheets-backend instructions are separate from current
production storage and do not authorize provider or production mutations.

## Documentation ownership

Maintain current ownership here and in the map, implementation rules in one guide,
operations in one runbook, next work in one roadmap, and historical results in one
evidence ledger. Verification contains commands/limits rather than per-release logs.
Use immutable links for archived detail. Keep user-guide paths and original source/
test fixtures stable; check links and consumers before consolidating documents.

tokens. The credential query uses the existing guarded transaction/connection.
All account IDs and consumer contracts remain unchanged. There is no automatic
fallback, credential endpoint or editor. Existing read-only deployments need only
metadata column grants. The synchronous legacy factory supports env and rejects

`infrastructure/external/google-auth` retains the exact shared Google auth classes
for Drive; the Sheets HTTP client and account row reader are retired. No active
runtime source reads a workbook. [Owner release/rollback procedure](../database-migration.md#private-account-configuration-release).

## Retired feature compatibility directory

The seven `src/features/backend/` forwards are removed. No business body moves: all other 414 production source/assets are byte-identical to main `2d2dc18a5c1112e9f6368599ad0d6d67defa79af` (merged PR43). The unused `@/feature/*` alias is removed; `@/*` continues targeting canonical source.

Existing fixtures stay immutable. Current loaders use physical owners and reject removed paths; explicit historical readers alone resolve archived sources. existing calculations/coercions, microsecond timestamp text, numeric scale,
creation ordering, media URL DTOs, session IDs and lazy business projections.
Root transport retains target/TLS/role checks, transactional revision handling,

# Architecture rules

## Folder ownership

Apply these rules to new and migrated code. `services` and standalone script leaves retain reviewed compatibility surfaces. `src/externals/` and `src/features/` are retired and must not be recreated. Do not scaffold empty layers or blindly move mixed files.

| Location under `src/` | Owns | Excludes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app/**/{page,layout,loading}.tsx` | Next routing, metadata, params, composition and required boundaries | Feature algorithms, reusable feature UI or browser clients |
| `app/api/**/route.ts` | Parsing, transport validation, response/error mapping and dependency construction/injection | Worksheet mapping and duplicate business rules |
| `app/globals.css`, route assets | Global reset/style, Next special assets | Movable feature CSS |
| `modules/<feature>/contracts.ts` | Named browser-safe public DTOs and runtime values with real consumers | Providers, server code, mixed barrels |
| `modules/<feature>/domain` | Framework-independent models and deterministic rules, only when needed | React/Next, config, IO, storage formats, implicit clock/random |
| `modules/<feature>/application` | Use cases and narrow consumer-owned ports | Concrete adapters, provider fetch, JSX, worksheet rows/ranges |
| `modules/<feature>/infrastructure` | Port implementations, feature worksheets/headers and row/response mapping | Duplicated generic transports or other features' private adapters |
| `modules/<feature>/server.ts` | Guarded, explicit named server composition | Browser exports or broad all-layer barrels |
| `modules/<feature>/ui` | Components/hooks, co-located CSS, formatters/PDFs and same-origin HTTP clients | Config, credentials, SDK/provider IO, server/application implementation imports |
| `infrastructure/persistence/postgres` | Server-only pooled transactions, durable command/effect transport and compatibility record projections supplied by feature bindings | Feature registries, business calculations, browser access or runtime fallback |
| `infrastructure/external/google-auth` | Shared Google OAuth/service-account token and JWT plumbing retained for Drive | Feature rules, worksheet schema or aggregate feature registry |
| `infrastructure/files/google-drive` | Drive provider/factory/protocol types, using shared Google auth | Order/movement policy |
| `infrastructure/external/{line,loyverse}` | Existing provider HTTP/signature/protocol/factory clients, including standalone operational LINE client | Feature journeys, worksheet reports and new providers |
| `infrastructure/configuration/postgres` | Read-only private integration-account metadata/credential SQL | Operational registry, public credential APIs, business rules or credential writes |
| `infrastructure/runtime` | Existing stateful sortable identifier implementation | Feature rules or duplicated sequence state |
| `composition` | Concrete aggregate construction and compatibility consumer wiring outside feature cores | Business algorithms, browser contracts, generic DI frameworks |
| `shared/{ui,lib,types}` | Proven generic reuse, small explicit utilities/value contracts | Feature dumping ground, config/infrastructure/module/legacy dependencies |
| `config` | Server configuration parsing/types | Feature rules, UI access, env renaming during moves |
| `scripts` | Explicit opt-in operational entrypoints | Automatic execution during verification |
| Root `tests` | Offline synthetic characterization, authoritative historical fixtures | Credentials, production records or automatic snapshot approval |

Root configuration/dependency files, `public` assets and existing operational guides keep their owners. Generic-looking employee, quantity, home and navigation components are not automatically shared. Keep feature contracts with their owner, not in `shared/types` just because another feature consumes them.

## Feature responsibility

| Module | Responsibility as migrations proceed |
| --- | --- |
| Orders | Draft/create/update/list/detail, bills, quantities, product codes/images; LINE journey state belongs to LINE workflows |
| Shipments | Shipment reads/creation/status, order links and bill coordination; consumes Orders contracts, does not own Order persistence |
| Inventory | Movements/delivery, monthly counts, reversals and adjustments; pure quantity parsing belongs here rather than LINE |
| Sales | Loyverse sync, receipts/refunds/reports and profit overrides; protocol client is root infrastructure |
| Expenses | Ledger/categories and current shop master; do not speculatively transfer shops to workspace |
| HR | Employee lifecycle, compensation, attendance, advances and settlement; consumes public sales/shop contracts when extracted |
| LINE workflows | Commands/replies/session/journeys; calls business use cases, never exports tokens or persistence details |
| Workspace | Home/breadcrumb/navigation; Sales owns its menu shell; global Next layout remains app-owned |

[Migration map](migration-map.md) records actual completed ownership and intentionally retained compatibility. Workspace/Next shell remains app-owned. Legacy business paths contain named forwards or identity bindings; concrete bridge functions now live in composition. Inventory owns movement schemas/quantity decisions, LINE owns sessions/journeys and external transport has root owners. All canonical adapters keep row/range mapping out of application ports.

The aggregate Sheets service remains a single composition object with its original constructor/health-check behavior. Its pure full-service declarations live in root `infrastructure/persistence/google-sheets/service-contracts.ts`; generic row types remain in `types.ts`. The former external indexes have no production replacements mixing transport and worksheets. Import concrete owners or named composition entrypoints. Do not move feature registry construction into root infrastructure.


## PostgreSQL migration ownership

`modules/<feature>/infrastructure/postgres/tables.ts` binds only that feature's
operational tables and existing headers to shared PostgreSQL transport. Existing
feature-owned port mappers remain the single mapping/calculation implementation.
The range-compatible projection stays in infrastructure; it is not a new domain
port or a parallel business service. `composition/postgres` owns the aggregate and
request transaction/auth/idempotency wrapper. The LINE module owns per-event
workflow execution/reply capture; shared transport only records/sends an effect
attempt. Operational schemas and offline promotion/profile tools live under
`supabase/migrations` and `tools/migration`. Immutable staging and mutable business
state have separate schemas and privileges. Current production selects PostgreSQL
through the approved release binding; isolated staging guards remain supported.
Former business Sheets are read-only, and Drive image ownership is unchanged.

`tools/migration` also owns explicit operator-only staging plans, private acceptance
reports, offline invocation of existing business readers, consistent logical backup
and restore evidence. These tools do not become runtime services or application
ports. Database tools require private PGSERVICE configuration; plugin identity is
not borrowed. Only synthetic fixture wrappers select disposable local databases.

## Dependency rules

Rules cover static/relative/alias imports, re-exports, erased types, import-type, dynamic import and require. An erased import can violate ownership; a legacy intermediary does not make private cross-feature access public.

| Importer | Allowed | Forbidden |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App server/explicit composition | Named public modules, config, root transport, concrete adapters required for wiring | Feature/storage algorithms in HTTP routes; active legacy runtime imports |
| Domain/application | Own contracts/rules/consumer ports, pure shared utilities, registered public consumer contracts/rules | Providers, concrete infrastructure/composition, legacy implementations, config/framework IO, implicit time/random |
| Feature infrastructure | Own ports/headers/mapping, root transport, registered public consumer contracts, erased root service interfaces | Another feature's private adapters, app/UI, mixed runtime barrels |
| Module UI/public browser contracts | Own/browser-safe registered contracts/UI, React/Next browser APIs and same-origin HTTP | Server/application/infrastructure/composition/config, Node/provider or legacy reachability, including erased paths |
| Root infrastructure | Generic transport/auth/protocol/runtime and supplied erased configuration types | Feature/schema/aggregate registry implementations or composition |
| Shared | Proven pure generic helpers/contracts | Features/app/config/infrastructure/composition/legacy dependencies |
| Config | Existing parsing/types using shared isRecord | Feature rules, provider execution or UI access |
| Compatibility | Exact named forwards/type/value identity bindings to canonical owners | Physical business functions/classes, duplicate state, broad barrels or forwarding cycles |

## Actual public surfaces and directions

- Orders contracts/rules/server own all order business surfaces; detail requires its own Shipment projection port. No Orders→Shipments or Orders→LINE module dependency. Shipments may use Orders contracts, the registered projection port and OrderImageGallery.
- Shipments has a single status enum, eight public DTOs, named server operations/error and public HTTP validation. Its browser client stays same-origin. Composition supplies the concrete Shipment detail projection outside Orders core.
- Inventory server alone composes public HR directory and Sales dashboard readers. Inventory application/domain receives semantic own ports. Its quantity public leaf exposes pure original rules to LINE; LINE never reads Inventory private worksheets directly.
- HR owns workforce/financial contracts and operations. Payroll receives HR-owned readers with public Sales data; SalaryAdvanceShops consumes the public Expenses shop projection. Concrete Sales/Expenses reader wiring lives in composition, not HR core.
- Sales receives Expenses data/public types and owns reports/receipt persistence. LINE core uses public Orders contracts/rules and Inventory contracts/quantity plus shared protocol DTOs/messages. Config/providers/aggregate service are injected at server/HTTP composition.
- Runtime module DAG: LINE workflows→Orders/Inventory, Inventory→HR/Sales, Shipments→Orders. Types add HR→Expenses and Sales→Expenses. Registered public leaves are contracts/server/status/quantity, LINE's specifically consumed Orders rules leaf, and the existing Shipment→Orders projection/gallery exceptions.

No module imports app/root composition. A public feature entrypoint may reach its own implementation; private dependencies across feature edges remain forbidden. Shared transport imports no feature even through erased declarations.

## Scoped enforcement

[Root ESLint config](../../eslint.config.mjs) registers the following existing rule sets. Their actual exact-path allowlists and shape checks are authoritative; this guide does not grant a broad module allowance.

| Rules | Protected boundary |
| --- | --- |
| [Orders browser](../../eslint/orders-boundaries.mjs) | Module UI rejects Shipment/app/legacy imports; picker port permits only Orders contracts. App OrderDetailClient allows exact detail/port, Shipment client and public enum imports, with no direct fetch/server/provider IO |
| [Shipment browser/contracts](../../eslint/shipments-boundaries.mjs) | All module UI forbids app/server/provider code; HTTP client allows erased own contracts plus browser fetch. Pure enum allows only exact enum declaration; contracts/legacy leaf require exact runtime/type export shapes |
| [Orders server](../../eslint/orders-server-boundaries.mjs) | Exact list/create/detail application/port/adapter/server imports; no concrete IO, direct Date/random/env in application, erased provider interfaces only where approved |
| [Shipment server](../../eslint/shipments-server-boundaries.mjs) | Separate exact creation/read/link/status/bill/projection scopes; no private Orders mapper. Only bill adapter permits original File/Buffer/Date conversion. Port/application exposes no transport types |
| [Shared Google](../../eslint/google-infrastructure-boundaries.mjs) | Exact seventeen root files, no feature/legacy implementation edges; Drive factory permits existing AppConfig as erased input only |
| [Orders pure Sheet prerequisite](../../eslint/orders-sheet-type-boundaries.mjs) | Orders worksheet/mapper avoid mixed aggregate Sheets type imports, including erased/relative bypasses |
| [Feature worksheets](../../eslint/worksheet-boundaries.mjs) | Exact Orders/Shipment/Sales/HR/Inventory class/header paths admit root BaseGoogleSheet, erased generic types, range utility and local headers only |
| [HR workforce](../../eslint/hr-workforce-boundaries.mjs) | Exact employee/attendance applications, semantic snapshot/reference ports, compensation/date rules, workforce adapter/runtime, HTTP imports and typed compatibility aliases |
| [HR financial](../../eslint/hr-payroll-boundaries.mjs) | Exact payroll/salary domain, application/ports, salary store, revision adapter, named server and explicit legacy reader composition; browser/HTTP exclusions |
| [Expenses business](../../eslint/expenses-boundaries.mjs) | Exact contracts/rules/ports/application/adapter/server/HR-reader scopes, browser imports and HR/Sales legacy/private import exclusions |
| [Employee directory](../../eslint/employee-directory-boundaries.mjs) | Exact Inventory/HR contracts/application/reader/query/composition; legacy adjustment/count/movement scopes reject mixed Sheets/private HR header paths |

Tests execute real flat-config positive/negative cases for alias, relative, erased, re-export, dynamic/require/import-equals/import-type bypasses, forbidden Node/framework/provider/config imports, direct global IO/time/random and exact public shapes. Required `server-only` markers protect new server compositions/adapters. Existing moved providers/worksheets do not gain markers that would alter original evaluation; browser reachability is tested instead.

ESLint direct-import rules do not prove transitive safety or cycles. TypeScript-resolved graph tests supplement them in runtime and runtime-plus-type modes, resolve re-exports, collapse intermediary paths for ownership, reject module/file cycles and inspect client reachability. Use [browser ownership helper](../../tests/helpers/browser-ownership.mjs) and relevant seam tests; do not silently expand closed offline loaders or global allowlists to make new code pass. Add tools/dependencies only in a separately justified tooling change.

Final scopes supplement the earlier exact guards: [Sales](../../eslint/sales-application-boundaries.mjs), [Inventory](../../eslint/inventory-application-boundaries.mjs), [Orders/LINE](../../eslint/orders-line-workflows-boundaries.mjs), [external transport](../../eslint/external-infrastructure-boundaries.mjs) and [final composition/compatibility](../../eslint/final-architecture-boundaries.mjs). The final independent rules reject active legacy imports and physical implementations in compatibility paths without overriding earlier application clock/dynamic/enum safeguards. Relocated physical composition retains its own explicit import/forwarding restrictions; remaining compatibility leaves allow only their named canonical owner. [External retirement](../../eslint/externals-retirement-boundaries.mjs) rejects retired imports in production and active tests, including erased, re-export, CommonJS, import-equals and statically folded dynamic paths. It also forbids recreating the directory and runtime/provider code in the pure root service-contracts leaf.

## Known legacy limits

All current browser graphs are clean in both modes; the inherited payroll type cycle is removed. Historical fixtures and restored-original negative graphs retain evidence of the old cycle/registry/browser paths. Exact source/hash inverses reconcile later moves before earlier guards run; independent current graphs inspect actual source, not those overlays.

The aggregate service/config interfaces live in the pure root `infrastructure/persistence/google-sheets/service-contracts.ts` leaf with identical declarations. Concrete construction lives only in explicit composition. Merged PR #40 removed all external indexes/forwards after the consumer audit; current tests load canonical owners and use test-only export projections for archived mixed-barrel identity evidence. Historical resolution is explicit and separate from strict physical current graphs. No generic repository, provider replacement, transaction/lock/retry/reconciliation policy or speculative Workspace redesign is introduced. Existing concurrency/partial-failure limitations remain; local graph/lint/fake-provider tests do not establish real provider availability, UI visuals, independent CI or authentication security.

## Loyverse account source boundary

[Scoped account guards](../../eslint/loyverse-accounts-boundaries.mjs) require server-only storage/composition, exact dependencies and a two-field pure metadata DTO. Consumers cannot read raw credential configuration, import the synchronous env-only factory or reach the private reader via alias, relative, erased or dynamic paths. HTTP composition receives metadata; Sales receives its existing ReceiptSource capability. No application/domain imports the new storage/composition implementation. Private Google failures discard provider bodies and client failures redact known tokens before HTTP/log handling. The actual current runtime/type/browser graphs remain independent of historical source inverses.

## Retired feature namespace

[Feature retirement guards](../../eslint/features-retirement-boundaries.mjs) reject live `@/features`, `@/feature` and relative feature-path imports in production and active tests, including erased, re-export, dynamic, CommonJS, import-equals and import-type forms. Recreating `src/features/` is forbidden. These independent rules supplement existing feature/Google/external/account safeguards without widening exceptions. The obsolete forwarding scope and singular alias are removed.

Historical graph hosts may resolve the seven archived paths for original/negative evidence only. Actual graph roots are physical current files; current import resolution, browser reachability, cycles, public module directions and canonical enum/function identities are verified separately. No application/domain or feature infrastructure dependency is added. Remaining service/script compatibility still requires its own consumer audit before retirement.


## Isolated PostgreSQL persistence

Application/domain ports and algorithms are unchanged. Feature-owned PostgreSQL
bindings import their own canonical headers and shared server-only record
transport; root infrastructure imports no feature registry. Composition chooses
the complete storage engine and provides one request-wide transaction. The LINE
server selects its own PostgreSQL event wrapper while retaining existing pure
applications. No browser graph may reach pg, pooled credentials or private
operational SQL. A staging-only public script retains operation keys and contains
no credentials. Exact route-body/factory/LINE/layout witnesses reconcile prior
history, while separate current-source, real-PostgreSQL and client-bundle checks
verify the actual new branch. Historical Sheets harnesses explicitly select their
original backend; they are not evidence of SQL behavior. Existing negative
ownership rules and all prior fixtures remain enabled and unchanged.


The stable-ID compatibility stage adds one exact root infrastructure bridge,

    items=json.loads((ROOT/'tests/fixtures/item-identity-before.json').read_text())
    references=json.loads((ROOT/'tests/fixtures/movement-reference-before.json').read_text())
    for name,expected in fixture['files'].items():

        upload_edit=uploads['edits'].get(name)
        if upload_edit:
            assert (digest(current) if current is not None else None)==upload_edit['afterSha256'],name
            current=upload_edit['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==upload_edit['beforeSha256'],name
        reference_edit=references['edits'].get(name)
        if reference_edit:
            assert (digest(current) if current is not None else None)==reference_edit['afterSha256'],name
            current=reference_edit['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==reference_edit['beforeSha256'],name
        item_edit=items['edits'].get(name)
        if item_edit:
            assert (digest(current) if current is not None else None)==item_edit['afterSha256'],name
            current=item_edit['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==item_edit['beforeSha256'],name
        session_edit=sessions['edits'].get(name)
        if session_edit:
            assert (digest(current) if current is not None else None)==session_edit['afterSha256'],name
            current=session_edit['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==session_edit['beforeSha256'],name
        revision_edit=revision['edits'].get(name)
        if revision_edit:
            assert (digest(current) if current is not None else None)==revision_edit['afterSha256'],name
            current=revision_edit['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==revision_edit['beforeSha256'],name
        bill_edit=bills['edits'].get(name)
        if bill_edit:
            assert (digest(current) if current is not None else None)==bill_edit['afterSha256'],name
            current=bill_edit['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==bill_edit['beforeSha256'],name
        account_edit=accounts['edits'].get(name)
        if account_edit:
            assert (digest(current) if current is not None else None)==account_edit['afterSha256'],name
            current=account_edit['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==account_edit['beforeSha256'],name
        delta=followup['edits'].get(name)
        if delta:
            assert current is not None and digest(current)==delta['afterSha256'],name
            current=delta['before'].encode()
            assert digest(current)==delta['beforeSha256'],name
        if edit:
            if edit['afterSha256'] is None:assert current is None,name
            else:assert current is not None and digest(current)==edit['afterSha256'],name
            data=edit['before'].encode()
        else:data=current
        assert digest(data)==expected,name
        dest=target/name;dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);dest.write_bytes(data)

    assert not list(target.glob('.env.*')) or {p.name for p in target.glob('.env.*')}=={'.env.example'}
